text: That night Ivan Ivanych could not sleep. <break time="0.8s" /> For through the wall. <break time="0.8s" /> He kept hearing his brother get up. <break time="0.8s" /> Go to the plate. <break time="0.8s" /> And take one more gooseberry. <break time="0.8s" /> He thought of all the misery. <break time="0.8s" /> Hidden behind quiet, happy homes. <break time="0.8s" /> The poverty, sickness, and suffering of the weak. <break time="0.8s" /> Which the contented simply chose not to see. <break time="0.8s" /> Behind the door of every happy man. <break time="0.8s" /> He thought. <break time="0.8s" /> There should stand someone with a little hammer. <break time="0.8s" /> Knocking constantly. <break time="0.8s" /> To remind him that unhappy people exist. <break time="0.8s" /> Ivan Ivanych then confessed. <break time="0.8s" /> That he, too, had once been satisfied with life. <break time="0.8s" /> Telling others. <break time="0.8s" /> That progress must come slowly. <break time="0.8s" /> And that they should be patient. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, gripping Alyohins hands. <break time="0.8s" /> He begged him. <break time="0.8s" /> Not to grow calm and contented. <break time="0.8s" /> While he was still young. <break time="0.8s" /> But to keep doing good. <break time="0.8s" /> As long as he lived. <break time="0.8s" /> If life has any meaning. <break time="0.8s" /> He said. <break time="0.8s" /> It lies not in our own happiness. <break time="0.8s" /> But in something far greater and more reasonable. <break time="0.8s" /> Neither Burkin nor Alyohin. <break time="0.8s" /> Was satisfied with the story. <break time="0.8s" /> For in that elegant room. <break time="0.8s" /> Where lovely Pelageya moved quietly about a poor clerk eating gooseberries. <break time="0.8s" /> Seemed tiresome. <break time="0.8s" /> They would rather have talked. <break time="0.8s" /> About elegant people and lovely women. <break time="0.8s" /> And at last Alyohin. <break time="0.8s" /> Sleepy after a long day of work. <break time="0.8s" /> Said good night and went downstairs. <break time="0.8s" /> Ivan Ivanych prayed for forgiveness. <break time="0.8s" /> And pulled the quilt over his head. <break time="0.8s" /> While Burkin lay awake. <break time="0.8s" /> Troubled by the stale smell of tobacco. <break time="0.8s" /> From his friends pipe. <break time="0.8s" /> And the rain beat against the windows all night.
